AAgent fundamentals

Chatbots, workflows
and agents

CHAT

Generate an answer

“Rewrite this message politely.”

The main result is text.
WORKFLOW

Follow known steps

“Validate a form, save it, send a receipt.”

The path is defined in code.
AGENT

Choose useful steps

“Find the right session and explain when it starts.”

The model may select a tool.
Key pointMany real apps combine fixed steps with model decisions.

  2. 02A tool checks the facts.
  3. 03The AI explains the result.

CContainers and project structure

Synchronous requests
and background jobs

SHORT TASK

Wait for the result

Question → API → answer. Stream text or progress while waiting.

Good for a small lookup.
LONG TASK

Track a job

Submit → job ID → worker → saved result. The screen checks progress.

Good for processing a large document set.
Key pointA queue organizes work. A cache speeds up access. Their jobs differ.
CContainers and project structure

Example project structure

agentic-app/
├── frontend/       # user interface
├── backend/
│   ├── api/        # requests
│   ├── agent/      # agent configuration
│   ├── tools/      # callable functions
│   └── services/   # data access
├── skills/         # skill definitions
├── evals/          # evaluation cases
├── infra/          # deployment configuration
├── .env.example    # environment variables
└── README.md       # setup instructions

Application components

Separate the user interface, API, agent logic and data access.

Configuration

Store environment variable names in .env.example and credentials outside Git.

Example directories

Directory names vary by project and framework.

EStreaming chat and artifacts

Streaming transports

TransportCommon useApplication responsibility
Fetch response streamPOST a prompt and read response chunksParse complete events; handle cancellation.
Server-sent events (SSE)Server sends named events over HTTPProvide event IDs and replay if needed.
WebSocketTwo-way messages on one connectionManage connection state and reconnects.

SSE is an event format; a fetch response can carry SSE.

Application events

Example eventMeaningUI update
run.startedBackend accepted the runShow pending state.
message.deltaMore text for one messageAppend to that message.
tool.started / tool.finishedA tool changed stateUpdate its activity indicator.
artifact.readyA saved output is availableShow an artifact card.
run.completed / failed / cancelledThe run reached a final stateStop the indicator; show the outcome.

EStreaming chat and artifacts

Cancellation
and reconnects

SituationExpected behavior
User selects StopCancel the reader and request backend cancellation.
Connection dropsShow disconnected state; reload status or replay events.
Client retries a requestReuse an idempotency key to avoid duplicate work.
Run fails after partial outputKeep the partial result marked incomplete; show retry.
Artifact takes longer than chatTrack it as a job and show a separate completion event.

FDemo stack and walkthrough

Tool permissions
and approval

READ

Look up a status

Check the user is allowed to see the record.

Use a bounded read-only tool.
DRAFT

Prepare a change

Show the proposed content or action.

Let a person review it.
COMMIT

Apply the change

Require the appropriate authorization and record the outcome.

Avoid repeating an action accidentally.
Key pointA prompt is guidance. Application code enforces permissions.
FDemo stack and walkthrough

Agent evaluation

CheckExample questionUseful evidence
CorrectnessDid it use the stored session time?Compare against known data.
HonestyDid it admit a missing session?No invented schedule entries.
BoundariesDid it stay within its allowed tool?Tool/event trace.
ExperienceWas it understandable and timely?Answer clarity and elapsed time.

latency and cost

CALL 1

Read the question

Model selects a tool.

→
TOOL

Fetch information

A service or database responds.

→
CALL 2

FDemo stack and walkthrough

Production checklist

AccessCheck identity and tool permissions.

DataChoose retention, backup and deletion.

FailuresHandle missing records and timeouts.

VisibilityRecord useful errors without secrets.

QualityRun realistic known and unknown cases.

CostSet limits and inspect actual usage.
